questions.question: What Shopify work do you usually take on?
questions.answer: Most projects fall into one of four buckets: custom theme work, Online Store 2.0 migrations, feature development for the storefront, and ongoing support after launch.

questions.question: Can you work inside an existing Shopify store?
questions.answer: Yes. I regularly work inside live Shopify stores to improve sections, product pages, cart behavior, filtering, integrations, speed, and launch readiness.

questions.question: Do you handle migrations to Shopify Online Store 2.0?
questions.answer: Yes. I can help move a store from a legacy setup to OS 2.0 while protecting content structure, rebuilding custom logic, and reducing launch risk.

questions.question: Can you help after launch too?
questions.answer: Yes. Many clients keep me involved after launch for fixes, experiments, SEO and speed improvements, new sections, and ongoing storefront development.

questions.question: How do we start?
questions.answer: Send the store URL, the problem you want solved, and any deadlines or constraints. From there I can suggest the cleanest next step, whether that is an audit, a small sprint, or a larger implementation.

questions.question: Do you work with designers or existing specs?
questions.answer: Yes. I can build from Figma, Loom videos, written specs, or an existing storefront reference, and I also help tighten the implementation plan when requirements are still rough.

anatomy.title: Anatomy of a store I build
anatomy.lead: Every Shopify store has the same five layers. Here is what I build in each of them, set up so your team can run it afterwards.

layers.title: Header & navigation
layers.text: Mega menus, search and a country and language switcher, built as theme sections your team edits without code.

layers.title: Pages from the design
layers.text: A Figma file or prototype turned into sections and blocks, matched to the design, with every text and image editable in the theme editor.

layers.title: Product logic
layers.text: Variant pickers, bundles, subscriptions and wholesale prices, driven by metafields and metaobjects instead of hard-coded templates.

layers.title: Cart & order value
layers.text: Cart drawers with free-shipping progress, upsells and gifts that add themselves once the cart reaches the threshold.

layers.title: Markets & data
layers.text: Prices and languages per country, and the events Klaviyo, search and analytics need, wired in and checked.
